card.title: T-60
card.text: Destruction: Add a T-34 1942 to your hand.
card.flavorText: The T-60 scout tank was a Soviet light tank that was used by the Red Army during WWII. The T-60 came into service in 1941 and was designed to replace the obsolete T-38 tank which had been in service from 1937. The original T-60 design came with a main armament of a 12.7 mm machine gun that was later replaced with a 20 mm TNSh cannon, which proved quite inadequate against newer German tank armor. The T-60 was not liked by their crews, to say the least, and some called it "a brother's grave for two" due to its disastrous performance on the battlefield. From 1941 to 1943 approximately 6000 T-60 tanks, including some variants, were produced, but they had more or less been pulled from frontline service in 1943 and mostly used for reconnaissance, convoy duties and training purposes. An unknown number of T-60 were captured by the Axis, some were converted to the German Panzerkampfwagen T-60 743(r).
